title: Wasm's LEB128 stores the lowest seven bits first
summary: The highest bit of the byte is 1, indicating that there is another group behind it. Unsigned e5 8e 26 represents 624485.
detail: Signed encodings check the last valid group of sign bits for extension. For example, 7f is −1 in sLEB and 127 in uLEB.
boundary: Wasm limits the maximum encoding length and the last group of unused bits for each bitwidth; arbitrarily long variants cannot be considered legal fields.
relevance: When reading immediate values or section lengths from modules, avoid interpreting signed constants as huge positive numbers.
